scope.title: Program Scope & Curriculum
scope.subtitle: A structured 10-month journey with 8 hands-on sessions every month.
scope.intro: Every month follows the same proven rhythm, taking students from understanding a component to building and evaluating a complete working project.

months.title: Month 1: Foundations of Electronics
months.text: Safety, breadboards, LEDs, resistors, and basic circuit thinking.

months.title: Month 2: Meet the Arduino
months.text: Arduino Nano/Uno architecture, IDE setup, digital output and first sketches.

months.title: Month 3: Sensors & Inputs
months.text: Buttons, LDR, ultrasonic and temperature sensors; reading the real world.

months.title: Month 4: Motion & Actuators
months.text: Servo and DC motors, motor drivers, buzzers, and controlled movement.

months.title: Month 5: Displays & Communication
months.text: LCD/OLED displays, serial communication, and Bluetooth basics.

months.title: Month 6: Robotics I
months.text: Line follower and obstacle-avoiding robot design and tuning.

months.title: Month 7: Internet of Things
months.text: Connected devices, dashboards, and remote monitoring and control.

months.title: Month 8: Smart Systems
months.text: Home and farm automation concepts using multi-sensor logic.

months.title: Month 9: Introduction to AI
months.text: Machine learning concepts, computer vision, and pattern recognition projects.

months.title: Month 10: Capstone & Showcase
months.text: Students design, build, and present an original project at a school expo.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers for school partners and parents.

items.q: What is the zero investment model for schools?
items.a: Schools invest nothing upfront. We provide the complete lab setup, kits, curriculum, and trained instructors. The program is sustained through a small monthly student fee.
The fee is ₹200 per student per month, covering kits, curriculum, instructor support, and assessments.

items.q: How is the hardware set up in the school?
items.a: Our team installs the lab in a room of your choice: workbenches, Arduino Nano/Uno kits, sensors, modules, and storage. We maintain and replace components throughout the year.

items.q: Which grades does the program cover?
items.a: Grades 1-12, with age-appropriate content: block-based and unplugged activities for younger learners, and Arduino, IoT, and AI projects for older students.

items.q: Do teachers need prior robotics experience?
items.a: No. Our trained instructors lead the sessions, and school teachers are welcome to learn alongside the students.
The program runs for 10 months with 8 sessions each month, fitting neatly into a regular school timetable.

items.q: How can our school get started?
items.a: Use the Contact Us page to request a free school demo. We will schedule a visit and walk you through the plan.
